meta.scope: EN-DE B2 Luna CRITICAL owner review preparation

findings.lunaClaim: Elster means magpie; hiccup is an entirely different word.
findings.reasonShort: DE Elster is the bird magpie; EN hiccup is Schluckauf, not Elster.
findings.independentValidation: German die Elster unambiguously denotes the bird (magpie). Latvian žagata confirms bird sense. English hiccup means a sudden involuntary throat contraction (German Schluckauf). There is zero semantic overlap. This is a wholesale wrong-word error, not a register or style issue. Luna proposal Magpie is correct and minimal.
findings.reason: Learners would associate Elster with the wrong English concept entirely. Replace lv with Magpie.

findings.deContent: das Gespött — mockery, ridicule; object of ridicule
findings.lunaClaim: Teething is unrelated; Gespött means mockery, ridicule or an object of ridicule.
findings.reasonShort: Gespött = ridicule/mockery; teething is infant dental eruption.
findings.independentValidation: Gespött (das) standardly means mockery, ridicule, or laughingstock. Teething describes babies cutting teeth — unrelated domain. LV zobošanās (grinning/baring teeth) may have misled the EN pipeline toward teeth/teething, but DE lemma is authoritative. Mockery is the correct minimal EN gloss for B2 vocabulary.
findings.reason: Current EN teaches the wrong noun entirely. Replace with Mockery (alternatives Ridicule acceptable but Mockery matches Luna and is natural).

findings.lunaClaim: Getriebe means gearbox or transmission; an engine is a different vehicle component.
findings.independentValidation: In automotive German, Getriebe is the gearbox/transmission assembly; Motor/Motorblock is the engine. LV master correctly has transmission term. EN The engine reverses the mechanical distinction learners need at B2. Gearbox is standard British EN; transmission also valid but gearbox is shorter flashcard gloss.
findings.reason: Semantically wrong component. Minimal fix: Gearbox (or Transmission if owner prefers US register — gearbox preferred for British EN course).

findings.lunaClaim: Spellbinding means fascinating; raffgierig means grasping, acquisitive or greedy.
findings.independentValidation: raffgierig combines raffen (grab) + gierig (greedy) → grasping, greedy, rapacious. Spellbinding means enthralling/fascinating — opposite evaluative direction. LV mantrausīgs confirms greedy/grasping sense. Acquisitive is accurate but slightly formal; Grasping is common B2 gloss. Luna Acquisitive acceptable; Grasping recommended as more direct.
findings.reason: Wrong adjective family entirely. Replace Spellbinding with Grasping (minimal, natural, matches DE collocation raffgierig sein).

findings.deContent: der Hahnenkamm — rooster's comb (fleshy crest on a rooster's head); also plant name cock's comb
findings.lunaClaim: The current expression is erroneous; Hahnenkamm means a rooster's comb.
findings.reasonShort: Hahn + Kamm = rooster's comb; Cock sext is corrupt/nonsense.
findings.independentValidation: Transparent German compound: Hahn (rooster) + Kamm (comb). Primary B2 sense is the rooster's head crest. EN Cock sext appears to be corruption from LV gaiļa sekste (likely erroneous LV gloss, sekste ≠ comb). The EN string is nonsensical and potentially offensive mis-parse. Rooster's comb is correct, pedagogically clear, British-appropriate.
findings.reason: Not a stylistic variant — current text is broken. Replace with Rooster's comb.

findings.deContent: der Hausrat — household goods, domestic furnishings, household contents (insured as Hausrat)
findings.lunaClaim: Hausrat means household belongings or goods; life is unrelated.
findings.independentValidation: Hausrat is a fixed German compound for movable household property (furniture, appliances) — familiar in insurance Hausratversicherung. Leben/life is unrelated. LV iedzīve (household belongings) confirms. Life is a single wrong noun with no polysemy bridge.
findings.reason: Replace Life with Household goods (minimal accurate gloss).

findings.deContent: das Herzversagen — heart failure (cardiac insufficiency); pump failure of the heart
findings.lunaClaim: Herzversagen means heart failure; cardiac arrest and insufficiency are not equivalent here.
findings.reasonShort: Herzversagen = Herzinsuffizienz; cardiac arrest = Herzstillstand (different emergency).
findings.independentValidation: Standard German medical usage: Herzversagen / Herzinsuffizienz = heart cannot meet circulatory demand (heart failure). Cardiac arrest (Herzstillstand) = mechanical/electrical cessation with no effective pulse — different pathology and emergency response. EN copied LV sirds apstāšanās (cardiac arrest) which misrenders DE. For vocabulary learning DE lemma is authoritative. Heart failure is the correct single gloss; Insufficiency alone is incomplete and arrest is wrong.
findings.reason: Medically misleading for learners. Replace with Heart failure. Note: LV master also mistranslates (DE_SOURCE in LV layer) but EN must follow DE.

findings.deContent: der Rain — agricultural field margin strip; uncultivated grass strip between fields or furrows (Feldrain/Ackerrain); NOT weather rain, NOT hedgehog
findings.lunaClaim: German Rain is a hedge or field boundary, not a hedgehog.
findings.reasonShort: Must remove hedgehog; exact agricultural EN term needs owner choice.
findings.independentValidation: German der Rain (homograph with rain weather) is an agricultural boundary strip (Feldrain): grass-covered margin between fields. LV eža = hedgehog — LV master error (confusion with Igel/ež). EN Hedgehog is completely wrong animal. Luna Hedge is also imprecise: hedge = Hecke/Gebüsch, not Rain. Valid EN glosses include field margin strip, field boundary strip, balk (technical), uncultivated field strip. Multiple are pedagogically defensible for B2; owner should pick one consistent term.
findings.reason: Status NEEDS_OWNER_REVIEW for exact replacement among valid agricultural EN terms. Provisional recommendation: Field margin strip. Reject Luna Hedge (semantically inaccurate for Rain). Reject keeping Hedgehog.
findings.ownerDecision: Choose standard flashcard gloss: Field margin strip vs Balk vs Field boundary strip vs Headland (latter less precise for Rain).

findings.deContent: das Richtfest — topping-out ceremony when roof timber/structure is complete (construction)
findings.lunaClaim: Richtfest is a ceremony marking completion of a building's roof framework, not a dragonfly festival.
findings.independentValidation: Richtfest from richten (align/set) + Fest — German construction celebration when main roof structure is erected. LV spāru svētki (rafter festival) aligns with topping-out. Dragonfly festival has no connection (Libelle/dragonfly unrelated to spāru). EN appears random corruption. Topping-out ceremony is standard British architectural gloss.
findings.reason: Replace Dragonfly festival with Topping-out ceremony.

findings.deContent: die Ringelnatter — grass snake (common European snake species)
findings.lunaClaim: Ringelnatter is the common grass snake, not an adjective meaning hungry.
findings.independentValidation: Ringelnatter is a specific snake (Natrix natrix). LV zalktis (lizard/grass snake) confirms animal. Hungry is adjective hungrig — no phonetic or semantic link. Wrong part of speech and wrong lexeme.
